summary: IMAP4rev1 (RFC 3501) is the mailbox-access protocol; 143 is cleartext with STARTTLS available, 993 is implicit TLS (IMAPS). Attacker value: harvesting credentials (LOGIN accepted pre-STARTTLS = sniffable plaintext), enumerating valid usernames (differential LOGIN/AUTHENTICATE responses, RFC 2971 ID leaks, SASL mechanism advertisements), fingerprinting mail-server products with well-known CVE histories (Dovecot pre-auth mem-disclosure, Cyrus RCE, Courier), and post-credential reading mail, staging drafts, and pivoting through shared mailboxes/GSSAPI to AD identity. recce currently has zero enum for this: nmap identifies it, svcdetect labels it, and serviceenum tags it as "pop-imap" but no handler exists. A dedicated stdlib module (imaplib + raw socket for the pre-auth commands imaplib will not send) closes the gap and feeds known_users / known_hostnames / known_domains / known_hashes.

existing_coverage.notes: nmap -sV names it; svcdetect confirms via `^\* OK.*IMAP` greeting regex; svcdetect._PRODUCT_RE extracts Dovecot/Courier/Cyrus product (but not always version) for the offline CVE mapper; serviceenum maps 143/993 -> "pop-imap" enum group. No dedicated probe module. No CAPABILITY/AUTH/STARTTLS/LOGINDISABLED introspection. No user-enum. No credentialed mailbox probe. No wiring into known_users/known_hostnames/known_domains/known_hashes.

capabilities.name: starttls_missing_on_143
capabilities.description: On 143/tcp, parse CAPABILITY reply for STARTTLS token (RFC 3501 §6.2.1) and flag when absent — every mailbox login on this listener crosses the wire in cleartext.
capabilities.notes: Send `A1 CAPABILITY\r\n`; look for `STARTTLS` in the untagged `* CAPABILITY` line.

capabilities.name: logindisabled_missing_pretls
capabilities.description: Before issuing STARTTLS, check whether the pre-TLS CAPABILITY response advertises LOGINDISABLED (RFC 3501 §6.2.3, RFC 2595 §4); its absence means the server accepts a plaintext LOGIN over the cleartext channel — the top IMAP finding.
capabilities.notes: Confirm by attempting LOGIN with a bogus username pre-STARTTLS: BAD/NO citing TLS = protected; NO 'invalid credentials' = plaintext accepted. Do NOT use real creds — the negative response alone confirms the exposure.

capabilities.name: sasl_mech_enum
capabilities.description: Parse CAPABILITY for every `AUTH=` token (RFC 3501 §7.2.1) to inventory mechanisms — PLAIN, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5, GSSAPI, NTLM, XOAUTH2, EXTERNAL, ANONYMOUS — each carries a distinct downstream (sniffable / offline-crackable / AD-relayable / anon-mailbox).
capabilities.notes: Emit one finding per weak mech: PLAIN/LOGIN over non-TLS = plaintext; CRAM-MD5/DIGEST-MD5 = offline-crackable (chain to known_hashes); GSSAPI = kerberos ticket relay; ANONYMOUS = free session; NTLM = SMB-relay chain.

capabilities.name: sasl_anonymous_login
capabilities.description: If AUTH=ANONYMOUS is advertised (RFC 4505), send `AUTHENTICATE ANONYMOUS` with a base64 trace token — a successful tagged OK opens an unauthenticated mailbox session and is a confirmed finding, not a probe.

capabilities.name: pre_auth_id_disclosure
capabilities.description: Issue `A1 ID NIL` in the pre-auth state (RFC 2971) — servers commonly leak `name`, `version`, `os`, `os-version`, `vendor`, `support-url`, and sometimes `command`, feeding CVE mapping and fingerprinting.
capabilities.notes: The reply is a parenthesised list of key/value strings; parse it, fold each field into the probe dict, and merge product/version into detect_source="banner".

capabilities.name: preauth_greeting_state
capabilities.description: The greeting can be `* PREAUTH ...` instead of `* OK ...` (RFC 3501 §7.1.4) — this means the transport (stunnel/local socket bridge, misconfigured proxy trust) already authenticated the session; treat as critical unauthenticated mailbox access.

capabilities.name: banner_product_version
capabilities.description: Extract product/version from the `* OK` greeting and the ID response (Dovecot, Cyrus IMAPd, Courier, MDaemon, Exchange, Zimbra) and feed the offline CVE DB — extend svcdetect._PRODUCT_RE to capture the version and to recognise Exchange/Zimbra/MDaemon.
capabilities.notes: Chains into recce's existing CVE mapper — no new code path, just a richer parse. Known-bad table example: Dovecot < 2.3.19.1 CVE-2022-30550 pre-auth memory disclosure; Cyrus IMAP < 2.5.17 CVE-2019-11356.

capabilities.name: tls_posture_993
capabilities.description: On 993/tcp inspect the TLS handshake (cert CN/SAN, notAfter, issuer, negotiated protocol/cipher) and flag SSLv2/SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 or expired certs; extract cert SANs/DN into known_hostnames/known_domains.
capabilities.notes: Reuse the TLS helpers already in recce/services/probes.py — 993 is in _COMMON_TLS_PORTS.

capabilities.name: user_enum_login_differential
capabilities.description: Probe a small curated user list against LOGIN and record response-code / timing differentials — a valid-user branch that takes materially longer or returns a distinct NO string discloses valid mail accounts (RFC 3501 §6.2.3).
capabilities.notes: Bounded 10-15 name list (root, admin, postmaster, mail, info, test, user, guest, backup, support) — same posture as smtp.enum_users. Union hits into recce.creds.known_users.

capabilities.name: default_creds_spray
capabilities.description: Try a small default-credential set (admin/admin, root/root, cyrus/cyrus, mail/mail, postmaster/postmaster, dovecot/dovecot) and any project defaultcreds hits against LOGIN — a tagged OK is a confirmed weak-cred finding and unlocks all downstream credentialed capabilities.
capabilities.notes: Hook into recce/creds/defaultcreds.py — that module already curates per-product defaults.

capabilities.name: credentialed_mailbox_enum
capabilities.description: Given a valid login, issue LIST "" "*", LSUB "" "*", NAMESPACE, GETQUOTAROOT, GETACL to enumerate every accessible mailbox, subscribed folders, and ACLs (RFC 3501 §6.3.8, RFC 2342, RFC 2087, RFC 4314) — reveals shared/public mailboxes accessible to this user.

capabilities.name: credentialed_message_search
capabilities.description: In a credentialed session run SEARCH against the inbox for password-reset / VPN-config / SSH-key / MFA-bypass patterns (RFC 3501 §6.4.4) — mail servers are high-yield loot and this converts one credential into wider network access; return hit list without downloading bodies.
capabilities.notes: Bounded SUBJECT/BODY search terms; return message IDs + sender + subject only. Never persist bodies without operator opt-in.

capabilities.name: starttls_downgrade_check
capabilities.description: After CAPABILITY, verify the server refuses commands other than STARTTLS/CAPABILITY/LOGOUT/NOOP in the pre-TLS state (RFC 3501 §11.1) — servers that accept AUTHENTICATE or LOGIN before STARTTLS enable downgrade even if LOGINDISABLED is advertised.

capabilities.name: gssapi_kerberos_relay
capabilities.description: AUTH=GSSAPI on an AD-joined mail server (Exchange, Dovecot with GSSAPI) advertises Kerberos — a relayable channel for ticket-forwarding or Silver-Ticket abuse; flag and cross-reference the hostname into known_hostnames as a relay target.

capabilities.name: cram_digest_challenge_capture
capabilities.description: If AUTH=CRAM-MD5 or DIGEST-MD5 is advertised, initiate the challenge, capture the server nonce, and record it for offline hashcat — the server-issued challenge means a captured client response is offline-crackable.
capabilities.notes: Feeds recce/creds/known_hashes.py — emit hashcat-mode 10200 (CRAM-MD5) with the challenge fragment.

recommended_findings.title: IMAP LOGIN accepted before STARTTLS (plaintext credentials)
IMAP PREAUTH greeting — unauthenticated mailbox session
IMAP does not offer STARTTLS on 143/tcp
IMAP weak SASL mechanism advertised (PLAIN/LOGIN over cleartext)
IMAP GSSAPI advertised — Kerberos relay surface
IMAP pre-auth ID response leaks server/product info (RFC 2971)
IMAP valid usernames enumerated via LOGIN differential
IMAP mailbox accessible with weak/default credentials (LIST/LSUB inventory)
IMAP inbox contains high-value loot (password reset / VPN / SSH key hits)
IMAP STARTTLS downgrade — AUTH accepted pre-TLS despite LOGINDISABLED

recommended_hashcat_modes.description: CRAM-MD5 — capture server nonce during AUTH=CRAM-MD5 negotiation

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_users — every valid mail account discovered via LOGIN differential, default-creds spray hit, or shared-mailbox owner extracted from LIST/GETACL; seeds SSH/SMB/AD/web spray downstream.
known_hostnames — server hostname from `* OK` greeting, RFC 2971 ID (`name`/`os`), and TLS cert CN/SAN on 993; feeds virtual-host discovery and Kerberos SPN construction.
known_domains — mail-domain part of any discovered account (user@domain), TLS cert SAN suffixes on 993, and NAMESPACE `Other Users/` shared-mailbox names; feeds OSINT/AD-domain enumeration.
known_hashes — CRAM-MD5 / DIGEST-MD5 server challenge + response pairs opportunistically captured; annotated with hashcat mode 10200 / 11500 for offline crack.
relay_targets — IMAP servers that advertise GSSAPI (Kerberos-relay surface) or NTLM AUTH= mechanism (SMB/HTTP-relay surface).

NEW SURFACE — mail_accounts (proposed): grouping of {SMTP submission user, IMAP user, POP3 user, mailbox-domain} across SMTP/IMAP/POP3 modules so a spray hit on one channel automatically re-tries the other two. Currently these three modules would learn the same accounts independently.
implementation_notes: Build recce/services/imap.py modelled on smtp.py: stdlib-only, use `imaplib.IMAP4` for 143 and `imaplib.IMAP4_SSL` for 993 (leverages the class's built-in CAPABILITY parsing and STARTTLS method), fall back to raw `socket` for pre-STARTTLS ID, CAPABILITY, and the plaintext-LOGIN detection dance because imaplib will happily send LOGIN over cleartext without a warning. Reuse svccommon.finding_builder + findings_to_vulns for consistent Vuln shape. Register the module in the enumerator (serviceenum currently tags 143/993 as "pop-imap" — either add an `imap` handler in that dispatch or split "pop-imap" into two entries). Extend svcdetect._PRODUCT_RE version-capture for Dovecot/Cyrus/Courier so the CVE mapper picks up e.g. `Dovecot ready.` -> `Dovecot 2.3.16`. Bounded runtime: ~4s per target (banner + CAPABILITY + ID + STARTTLS + plaintext-LOGIN probe + optional 15-user enum bounded to ~5s more). All operations are read-only — no APPEND, no STORE, no mailbox modifications. Reuse recce/services/probes.py TLS helpers on 993 (already in _COMMON_TLS_PORTS).
